searchText: Hey <@848067664177790976>, I'm from Kurtosis and we are building devOps tools for web3 - feel free to DM me for any questions about the above or if you have other ideas you'd like to try 🙂 have a doubt regarding SSZ: when i encode a struct with a field of type string with fastssz, i get an overflow error, is it because a string is an unbounded type which ssz can't encode? i see most ssz encoded structs as fixed size byte arrays ssz doesn't have the notion of "string", you have either vectors of fixed size, or lists with a limit size (the limit is typically something unrealiistically high, but just there for merklizing purposes. I am assuming that by "string" on fastssz you are thinking on a byte slice, and then you need to merkleize it with an ssz limit. understood, so basically i cannot have a struct like: `type Example struct { field1 string field2 uint64 }` no, you need to specify a limit for `field1`, string is not an ssz type because field1 has no limit in size, i can make field1 a byte slice with an ssz limit which can be provided in the field tags if im right got it this is clear! Is there any fellowship in CT or NYC coming up? would love to join, cheers I just opened a PR with my new project proposal. https://github.com/eth-protocol-fellows/cohort-four/pull/293 Any feedback would be greatly apreciated `:)` cc <@686695036733227017> <@914307919699406908>

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: ssz doesn't have the notion of "string", you have either vectors of fixed size, or lists with a limit size (the limit is typically something unrealiistically high, but just there for merklizing purposes. I am assuming that by "string" on fastssz you are thinking on a byte slice, and then you need to merkleize it with an ssz limit.
